story.title: Ireland to Boycott Eurovision Again Over Israel's Participation Amid Gaza Conflict
story.summary: Ireland's national broadcaster has announced a boycott of the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest for the second consecutive year. The decision is in protest against Israel's participation, citing the ongoing loss of lives in Gaza as a significant factor. Ireland joins other countries, including the Netherlands, Iceland, Slovenia, and Spain, in this protest.

event_overview.title: About Eurovision Song Contest
event_overview.subject: Eurovision Song Contest
event_overview.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest is an annual international live music competition in which participating public-service broadcasters enter songs and artists, co-producing televised shows under the auspices of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU). First staged in Lugano, Switzerland, on 24 May 1956, it has developed into a major cross-border television event built around musical performance, voting and broadcaster collaboration.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: The first Eurovision Song Contest took place on 24 May 1956 at the Teatro Kursaal in Lugano, Switzerland, with artists representing seven broadcasters.

facts.label: Governing and production model
facts.value: The Contest is an international entertainment event co-produced by broadcasters that are EBU members, with the EBU organizing it; participating broadcasters are the EBU members that enter a contestant.

facts.label: Participation
facts.value: Participation is based on broadcasters rather than national governments. EBU membership is open to qualifying broadcasting organizations in the European Broadcasting Area or Council of Europe member states, and members may participate in the Contest.

facts.label: Competition format
facts.value: Recent editions use two semi-finals and a Grand Final: in 2026, 30 broadcasters competed in semi-finals, with the top 10 from each progressing to the final; the final result combined jury and audience voting.

facts.label: 2027 edition
facts.value: The 71st Contest is scheduled for Arena Burgas in Burgas, Bulgaria, with semi-finals on 11 and 13 May and the Grand Final on 15 May 2027; Bulgarian National Television (BNT) is the host broadcaster working with the EBU.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the 2027 host-city decision and reported broadcaster boycott decisions through 17 September 2026; it does not provide a complete history of the Contest, every participating broadcaster, or all political and programming developments surrounding the edition.

explore_lenses.label: What conditions in Gaza drove RTÉ’s decision?
explore_lenses.title: Continuing casualties and humanitarian strain
explore_lenses.summary: RTÉ tied its withdrawal to ongoing civilian deaths, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and limits on independent international media access. Recent UN reporting describes continued attacks, displacement and severe pressure on basic services despite a ceasefire agreement announced in October 2025.

claims.text: RTÉ said it could not justify participation or broadcasting the 2027 contest because of the continuing loss of life in Gaza, the humanitarian crisis and its concern about continued denial of independent access for international journalists.
OCHA reported that Israeli airstrikes and other attacks were continuing to hit populated areas in Gaza, causing casualties, property damage and further displacement.

OCHA reported that 91% of assessed Gaza households faced moderate to high water insecurity, while overcrowding, inadequate shelter and limited water and sanitation access were increasing disease risks.

explore_lenses.label: How did Eurovision’s dispute reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A second year of broadcaster protests
explore_lenses.summary: Ireland’s decision follows a 2026 boycott by five broadcasters and a separate August 2026 decision by Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS to stay out again. The broadcasters’ stated concern is that Israel’s participation during the conflict has undermined the contest’s claimed neutrality; the EBU has pursued rule and process changes but the Dutch broadcaster says they did not resolve that concern.

claims.text: Ireland, the Netherlands, Iceland, Slovenia and Spain did not take part in Eurovision 2026 in protest over Israel’s participation, according to reporting on RTÉ’s new decision.

AVROTROS said its 2027 withdrawal was based on its view that Eurovision could no longer be considered neutral while a participating country remained involved in a large-scale military conflict; it cited humanitarian suffering in Gaza and press-freedom restrictions.
AVROTROS said it had sought transparent participation rules from the EBU, but judged the EBU’s recently announced changes insufficient to restore the contest’s independent and neutral character.
The EBU has said it remained committed to finding ways for the five members that skipped the 2026 contest to return in 2027.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed for Eurovision 2027?
explore_lenses.title: Ireland will neither enter nor air the contest
explore_lenses.summary: Ireland’s withdrawal does not stop the 2027 contest: the EBU and Bulgarian National Television have set dates and a host city. RTÉ has confirmed both non-participation and non-broadcasting, while the EBU says broadcasters make participation decisions annually and remains in dialogue with RTÉ.

claims.text: RTÉ confirmed it will neither participate in nor broadcast Eurovision 2027.
The EBU has scheduled Eurovision 2027 in Burgas, Bulgaria: semi-finals on 11 and 13 May and the final on 15 May, at Arena Burgas.

Eurovision director Martin Green said the EBU regretted but respected RTÉ’s decision, and that broadcasters decide annually whether to enter the following year; he said the EBU hoped RTÉ would return.

story_report.summary: Ireland’s public broadcaster, RTÉ, will not take part in or broadcast the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest, extending its protest over Israel’s participation for a second consecutive year. RTÉ said the continuing loss of life in Gaza, the humanitarian crisis and restrictions on independent international-media access meant it could not justify involvement. The withdrawal removes Ireland from the contest scheduled for May in Burgas, Bulgaria, while the final participant list remains unsettled.

sections.heading: Gaza conditions cited by RTÉ
sections.body: RTÉ framed its decision as a response to the humanitarian consequences of the war in Gaza and its concern over continued denial of independent access for international journalists. Separately, the UN humanitarian office OCHA reported that Israeli airstrikes and other attacks continued to strike populated areas, causing casualties, damage and displacement. OCHA also said 91% of assessed Gaza households faced moderate to high water insecurity, with poor shelter, overcrowding and limited water and sanitation increasing disease risks.

sections.heading: Eurovision withdrawals and return prospects
sections.body: Ireland was among five countries — alongside the Netherlands, Iceland, Slovenia and Spain — that did not participate in Eurovision 2026 in protest over Israel’s inclusion. Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS has also confirmed a 2027 withdrawal, saying it no longer viewed the contest as neutral while a participant was involved in a large-scale military conflict, and that EBU rule changes were insufficient. The EBU has said it hopes the five members that skipped the 2026 event will return, while Eurovision director Martin Green said the organization respected RTÉ’s decision.

sections.heading: Burgas prepares for Eurovision 2027
sections.body: The EBU has scheduled the 2027 contest at Arena Burgas in Bulgaria, with semi-finals on 11 and 13 May and the final on 15 May. Broadcasters decide annually whether to enter the following year, according to Green. RTÉ’s decision is confirmed, but the evidence reviewed does not establish whether Iceland, Slovenia or Spain will join Ireland and the Netherlands in withdrawing from the 2027 contest.

unresolved.text: The final list of Eurovision 2027 participants, including whether Iceland, Slovenia and Spain will withdraw or whether other broadcasters will return, has not been confirmed in the reviewed sources.

related_stories.title: Mbappé Addresses Controversy Over Ceuta Solidarity T-Shirt
related_stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé explained his decision to partially roll up a t-shirt supporting Ceuta residents, stating it was meant to express solidarity with migrants who have lost their lives and those facing difficult conditions. His action has drawn criticism from far-right politicians in Spain and France, who interpreted it as a rejection of Ceuta and its residents.

related_stories.title: U.N. Experts Find Grounds to Believe U.S. Committed War Crimes in Iran Strikes
related_stories.summary: A United Nations fact-finding mission has concluded there are reasonable grounds to believe that the United States committed war crimes during two military strikes in Iran in February. These strikes targeted a school and a sports facility, resulting in significant civilian casualties, including the deaths of 156 civilians, among them 120 children. The findings suggest that these actions may constitute violations of international law.
